From the s9 local cleanup (2026-11-01; ~/hpo-orch/cleanup-20261101.log). The disk was at 7.8 GiB free, under the sweep's 15 GiB floor, so the sweep ran tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh, which reported "eligible 0, kept 131". A hand cleanup that proved each item dead then freed 10.2 GiB: 30 worktrees, plus 61 plain repo copies totalling 4.9 GiB. worktree_gc missed them for three reasons:
(1) It keeps every branch that has no pull request of its own, and fixer branches (`work/*`, `scratch/*`, `seat/*`) never do, because their PR sits on `fix/<topic>`.
(2) Its orphan-dir class defaults to /tmp/hpo-orch, but seats live under ~/hpo-seats/<round>.
(3) It has no class for plain repo copies (mutant, null and head trees with no .git) inside seat dirs.
Fix:
- Map a seat branch to its PR topic; a merged or closed PR makes the seat eligible, once it has no unpushed commits, a clean status and no live process.
- Read the seats root from config or the environment.
- Add a class for plain copies under a seat dir whose topic's PR is merged.
- Keep the safety gates the cleanup used: an lsof/ps cwd check, no unpushed commits, clean status.
Failing test first: a fixture seat on a merged topic, eligible after the fix and kept today. Null control: a seat with one unpushed commit, or with a live process cwd in it, stays kept. [moved: R10-CLOSEOUT-INSTRUMENTS]

groups.brief:
Programme-closeout work, and it runs LAST: after R10-ARCH-DOCS and R10-ROUND-PLAYBOOK have merged, after the roster and the state docs have moved into main, and before the closure stamp. Owner request (tvofi, 2026-10-24): the programme must contain a group that cleans up after itself and drives the open branches down to the owner's 1-3 target. Round-10 end state: main plus at most two development branches, remote and local, every other ref archived as a tag first, GitHub's merged pull request branches already deleted. This group is the single owner of that end state; R10-FLY-PRUNE-REFS owns only the two defects in tools/audit/seat/prune_refs.py and must land first, so this group uses prune_refs.py as its ref instrument and never a session-local loop (decision 0013).

Deliver a self-tested closeout instrument under tools/audit/seat/ that composes the existing instruments (tools/audit/seat/prune_refs.py, tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh, tools/audit/seat/state_docs.py) and is a dry plan by default, acting only under --apply, with the ordering below written as code. Then run it with --apply as the final act of the round (the orchestrator's step; the pull request lands the instrument and its fixtures, the run leaves the end state and the report). Steps, each gated by the one before:
(1) Move the roster and the state docs into main, because the roster branch and the state ref are read at run time and must not be deleted while a workflow or a citation reads them (see the R9-CLOSURE-BRANCHES brief in dev/programme/rosters/wave-r9-groups.json for the hazard list). Sweep in-tree citations of every ref family about to go and retarget each to the archive tag at the same sha; prove it with node tools/policy/brief_lint.mjs (dev/governance/rules/brief-citations.md).
(2) Archive before delete: every remaining handoff/*, handoff-body/*, fix/*, design/*, review/*, probe/*, claim/*, dispatch/* and record/* ref (and the other families prune_refs.py enumerates, verdict/* only once --verdicts-drained) is retagged under archive/<family>/<name> at its own commit, then its branch is deleted. origin keeps main plus at most two branches. Derive the counts with git ls-remote and a prefix histogram; carry none.
(3) Local state: remove every seat worktree under ~/hpo-seats and under ~/.local/state/hpo/pr (a worktree holding an unpushed commit is reported and kept until the owner rules; worktree_gc.sh must already leave such a worktree alone, which is R10-FLY-WORKTREE-GC); clear scratch under ~/hpo-orch except the final ledger and state; prune git worktrees; reduce local branches to main plus at most two; run a final worktree_gc.
(4) Issues and sessions: close or disposition every open issue except the coordination issue's successor, each with the number that closes it or the re-scope that keeps it; archive merged cloud sessions.
(5) Closure report: write counts before and after for refs by family, tags added, worktrees, local branches, open issues and open pull requests, plus every ref left and the rule that kept it, to the round-10 evidence directory under dev/audit/rounds/.
Controls: a fixture where a ref to be deleted lacks its archive tag must refuse (every tag precedes every delete); an open-PR ref and main are kept (null control); a worktree with an unpushed commit survives; a dry run writes nothing. Spare the API: batch ref writes (R10-FLY-PRUNE-REFS carry (i)). Part of #201.

NULL CONTROL, owed as tests: on a trace with no cycle shorter than the sample period the counted starts, and so the cycling cost and the plan, are identical before and after. Positive case: a trace with a stop and restart inside one sample period counts one more start than today. An unavailable or non-numeric signal counts nothing. Not verified by triage: the sample cadence and the contributor's own count of missed starts; measure both before claiming a figure. The pull-request body thanks Bankaifan by name and pull request 3420. Every quantified claim carries its null control. Defect: tools/pr/prepr.sh ancestry_reds (line 1401 at origin/main 5345766b41) reads repos/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs with --paginate once for every commit of merge-base..<remote head>, and on an all-green branch reads each commit a second time for total_count. The call count therefore grows with the branch's ancestry, not with its CI runs. Evidence: on the round roster pull request (about 777 commits over its merge base) one update attempt read 767 calls in 6.6 min (orchestrator sweep 2026-11-12T23:36Z); two update_pr runs on that pull request made 3482 gh calls in under an hour (sweep 2026-11-13T05:10Z), which is about 70 % of the 5000-call core bucket the host's seats share; the bucket read 0 twice (23:3xZ and 00:05Z, reset 00:27:36Z), and the merge train stopped rc=1 at 00:04:23Z unable to read required contexts, merging nothing. Fix: bound the read by what can hold a red the branch must answer. Candidates to measure, not to assume: read only commits that carry a pull_request or push run (one runs listing per branch instead of one call per commit), stop at the first N commits from the head, or cache per-sha reads under the state directory since a check run at a fixed sha only gains entries. Whatever is chosen, an unread commit stays UNCHECKED, never confirmed empty (the function's existing fail-closed rule). Control the fixer must show: the call count of one prepr run on a long-ancestry fixture branch (at least 500 commits, a stub gh counting calls through PREPR_GH) before and after, with after more than 20 % below before (the owner's bar) and the ratio stated; the same red name list on a fixture whose red sits on an ancestor commit, before and after (no answered red lost); null control: a branch of 3 commits makes the same number of calls or fewer. groups.brief: AUDIT-CLASS BARRIER, part C of the root-cause analysis R10-RCA-SELFTEST-SCOPE-DRIFT (triage ACCEPT, round 10). Start only after R10-HOTFIX-SELFTEST-SCOPE-RERECORD has merged; base on that main. Cause being closed: the measured table tools/ci/selftest_closures.json is repaired by hand re-records, and the record subcommand of tools/ci/selftest_scope.py replaces a step's entry with one recording (at origin/main the record function ends by starting from the old steps only under --step, else from an empty dict, then updating with the new measurement), so a re-record taken at a stale base drops reads main measures. Merges #3409, #3419 and #3506 dropped 660, 8 and 10 entries; 6 of the 20 drift refusals at f47250150a were such drops. Two changes. (1) record unions: in both the per-step and the whole-table mode it keeps every read the committed entry holds and adds the new measurement; removing a read becomes a separate, explicit operation the operator must name. Over-approximation is already documented as safe in the tool's header. (2) A table-shrink guard: when a diff changes the table, refuse every files, probes, dirs or git item, and every index or objects flag, that the head's entry drops relative to the base's entry for the same step, unless the same diff deletes that path; a step removed from the workflow is not a drop. Put the guard in the existing static subcommand, which governance.yml already runs in the scope's own self-test step on every pull request that touches the table (the table is in GATE_FILES, so that run is FULL); do not edit any workflow and do not add a job step. On a push to main compare against the first parent. Because the guard reads the base's table, the self-test step's measured reads change: re-record that step on Linux with strace, by the new union record, in this same pull request, and show the drift check clean for it. Tests: a failing test first for each change (recording one step over an entry holding a read the new trace lacks keeps that read; a fixture diff that drops an entry is refused and one that deletes the path is not). Mutants in tools/ci/selftest_scope_mutants.sh, each killed: restoring the replace semantics; removing the deletion exemption. Demonstration the body must show: the guard over every first-parent merge that touched the table from ba6fd7e8b0^ to f47250150a refuses exactly #3409, #3419 and #3506 and passes the other 12, including #3507 (its deletion is exempt); that is the null control, it must neither fire on additive merges nor skip. Then list its result on every later table-touching merge up to the base, the RERECORD merge included, and explain any it refuses. Add one class for this mechanism to dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json naming the RCA, so tools/audit/fold_ledger.py check tracks it; part A (main re-records mechanically) is ruled to round 11 and is not this group. No budget raise; re-check the ratchets. Cutoff: if this group has no pull request in review by 2026-11-14T18:00Z the orchestrator moves it to round 11; do not let it hold the round-10 closure.

Defect: tools/pr/prepr.sh ancestry_reds (line 1401 at origin/main 5345766b41) reads repos/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs with --paginate once for every commit of merge-base..<remote head>, and on an all-green branch reads each commit a second time for total_count. Evidence: on the round roster pull request (about 777 commits over its merge base) one update attempt read 767 calls in 6.6 min (orchestrator sweep 2026-11-12T23:36Z); two update_pr runs on that pull request made 3482 gh calls in under an hour (sweep 2026-11-13T05:10Z), which is about 70 % of the 5000-call core bucket the host's seats share; the bucket read 0 twice (23:3xZ and 00:05Z, reset 00:27:36Z), and the merge train stopped rc=1 at 00:04:23Z unable to read required contexts, merging nothing. Fix: bound the read by what can hold a red the branch must answer. Candidates to measure, not to assume: read only commits that carry a pull_request or push run (one runs listing per branch instead of one call per commit), stop at the first N commits from the head, or cache per-sha reads under the state directory since a check run at a fixed sha only gains entries. Whatever is chosen, an unread commit stays UNCHECKED, never confirmed empty (the function's existing fail-closed rule). Control the fixer must show: the call count of one prepr run on a long-ancestry fixture branch (at least 500 commits, a stub gh counting calls through PREPR_GH) before and after, with after more than 20 % below before (the owner's bar) and the ratio stated; the same red name list on a fixture whose red sits on an ancestor commit, before and after (no answered red lost); null control: a branch of 3 commits makes the same number of calls or fewer. groups.brief: Owner instruction 2026-11-14, his words: "Have a fable seat with web access and sendmessage capability study and design a high throughput pipeline, using a branch parallel with main. Study publicly available designs and standards. The design should be planned and built (if it will save significand wall clock time in a programme) before the fixers in round 11 start." Design first (decision 0014): a study of the published merge-queue, merge-train, gating and batch-integration designs and of the delivery standards that measure them; a measured baseline of where this programme's wall clock goes between a fixer's handoff and its merge on main in round 10; then a pipeline design in which reviewed work is integrated continuously on a branch that runs parallel with main and main advances only to states that integration has proved, with its failure handling, its interaction with the scoped gate, the structural ratchets, the claim files, the stamp, the identity rules and the review freeze stated. The design carries a cost test in wall-clock hours per programme against the measured baseline with its null control, and the build is dispatched only if that test shows a significant saving and the design review approves; a design that does not pay records that result and builds nothing. Constraints the owner has already ruled: no proposal that widens CI capacity by billing, runners, plan or a second account; main's protection and the required gate are not loosened; policy changes go to the owner's review. The design and any prototype live on refs beside main and touch nothing on main; nothing of this group starts a CI run before the round-10 closure stamp without the orchestrator's word, and it never takes a seat, a reviewer or CI priority from round-10 production work. If built, the build parts land after the round-10 closure stamp and before the round-11 fixers start. Fable seats for the designer, the design review and the build (owner ruling 2026-11-11 for L and XL work).

triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch202.md#P628 at ca76b1d0cf

Instrument fix, S. The merge train's step 6, approve() in tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py, posts the approver App's approval at the head right before the merge. That approval starts a `CI review` run of ci.yml, whose pending `gate` blocks the merge under base-branch policy, so review_settle() waits for it. Measured from train.log on 2026-11-11: 11 of 22 merges waited, 2800-6100 s in total. Under runner saturation the waits were 23-28% of the train's time over 11:13Z-14:05Z and 63-96% of each waiting entry (#3453 1020-1320 s, #3447 1320-1620 s). Null control: none of the 50 completed review runs turned a green head red.

The fix: when a batch starts, after any up-front recarry, approve once each entry whose head passes steps 1-5 (verdicted, CARRY yes, main inside, gate green, policy/mandate and budget-raise checks) and is not already approved, so its review run runs while earlier entries merge. Step 6 at merge time then finds the approval at the head and posts nothing (the existing once-per-head rule). A head that moves is approved afresh at its turn, as today. An entry failing any pre-approval check is left to step 6 unchanged. ci.yml is not touched.

Acceptance (selftest): (i) N eligible entries are each approved once at batch start, and approve() at merge returns `already, at this head`; (ii) a moved head is re-approved at its turn; (iii) a CARRY-no, red, unverdicted, policy-without-mandate or budget-raise entry is not pre-approved; (iv) null control: with a one-entry batch, the call order is unchanged from main; (v) mutants: dropping the pre-approval makes (i) red (the stub review run has not concluded at the entry's turn), and pre-approving a CARRY-no entry makes (iii) red; (vi) replay of today's #3453/#3447 timeline: their review runs start at batch start, not at 13:38:09Z.
